title: Greater end of the interval for |x-a| < b
source: P23 Ch1 theory P23-1.3 Quick check 1 (|x-3|<5, greater end 8)
stem: Solve the inequality \(\lvert x-{a|int}\rvert\lt {b|int}\). What is the greater end of the solution interval?

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: The inequality is equivalent to \(-{b|int}\lt x-{a|int}\lt {b|int}\), so \({a|int}-{b|int}\lt x\lt {a|int}+{b|int}\).
steps.note: Rewrite |x-a| < b as a pair of linear inequalities.

steps.name: E
steps.text_tex: The greater end of the interval is \({E|int}\).

contexts.stem: The inequality \(\lvert x-{a|int}\rvert\lt {b|int}\) describes an interval of values of \(x\). Write down the greater end of that interval.
On a number line, \(\lvert x-{a|int}\rvert\lt {b|int}\) is the open interval centred at {a|int}. What is the greater end of this interval?

title: Greater end of the interval for |cx-d| < k
source: P23 Ch1 theory P23-1.3 Quick check 2 (|2x-1|<7, greater end 4)
stem: Solve the inequality \(\lvert {c|int}x-{d|int}\rvert\lt {k|int}\). What is the greater end of the solution interval?

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: The inequality is equivalent to \(-{k|int}\lt {c|int}x-{d|int}\lt {k|int}\). Adding {d|int} and dividing by {c|int} gives the upper end \(({d|int}+{k|int})/{c|int}\).
steps.note: Rewrite as a pair of linear inequalities and rearrange.

steps.name: E
steps.text_tex: The greater end of the interval is \({E|int}\).

contexts.stem: Find the greater end of the solution of \(\lvert {c|int}x-{d|int}\rvert\lt {k|int}\).
Solve \(\lvert {c|int}x-{d|int}\rvert\lt {k|int}\) and write down the greater end of the resulting interval.

title: Smaller boundary value of |x-a| >= b
source: P23 Ch1 theory P23-1.3 Quick check 3 (|x-6|>=2, smaller boundary 4)
stem: Solve the inequality \(\lvert x-{a|int}\rvert\geqslant {b|int}\). What is the smaller of the two boundary values of the solution?

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: The inequality is equivalent to \(x-{a|int}\leqslant -{b|int}\) or \(x-{a|int}\geqslant {b|int}\), so \(x\leqslant {E|int}\) or \(x\geqslant {hi|int}\).
steps.note: Rewrite |x-a| >= b as two linear inequalities.

contexts.stem: The solution of \(\lvert x-{a|int}\rvert\geqslant {b|int}\) consists of two unbounded rays. What is the smaller of the two boundary values?
Solve \(\lvert x-{a|int}\rvert\geqslant {b|int}\) and write down the smaller boundary value.

source.note: Stem verbatim from the QP PDF (modulus bars checked on the rendered page; pdftotext had flattened them). Steps and marks from the official MS PDF (page 6). Independently: the boundary values are x=-3/4 and x=7/2, and the inequality holds between them. Fully manual, because the official answer is an interval.

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: State or imply the non-modular inequality \((3x-2)^2\lt(x+5)^2\), or the corresponding equation or pair of linear equations \(3x-2=\pm(x+5)\).
steps.note: MS: B1 State or imply non-modular inequality (3x-2)^2 < (x+5)^2 or corresponding equation or pair of linear equations.

steps.name: att
steps.text_tex: Attempt the solution of the resulting 3-term quadratic equation, or of the two linear equations.
steps.note: MS: M1 Attempt solution of 3-term quadratic equation or of 2 linear equations.

steps.name: cv
steps.note: MS: A1 Obtain critical values -3/4 and 7/2.

steps.name: ans
steps.note: MS: A1 State answer -3/4 < x < 7/2. (Alternative route: B1 for 7/2 from a graph, inspection or equation; B2 for -3/4 similarly; B1 for the same final interval.)

steps.text_tex: State or imply the non-modular inequality \((4-5x)^2\lt 3^2\), or the corresponding equation or pair of linear equations \(-3\lt 4-5x\lt 3\).
steps.note: MS: EITHER M1 State or imply non-modular inequality (4-5x)^2 < 3^2, or corresponding equation or pair of linear equations.
